sections.vendors: John Lewis launched a new Mirakl-powered Supplier Operating Platform designed to speed up onboarding of hand-picked brands, with luxury footwear specialist Russell & Bromley named as one of its first partners. The retailer still runs a base of over 2,000 tier-one own-brand supplier factories across its established sourcing network.
sections.sustainability: No new certification announcements this week; JLP's stated 2026 priorities remain getting suppliers ready for the incoming EU Forced Labour Regulation and refreshing deforestation- and conversion-free raw material roadmaps. Its Better Jobs supplier support projects in India and China continue as the main active supply-chain welfare initiative.
sections.sourcing: No new nearshoring or country-shift announcements specific to JLP surfaced this week. India remains a core focus via the Better Jobs programme alongside China, while the wider UK apparel industry continues drifting toward Turkey, Portugal and Morocco for speed-to-market nearshoring — a trend JLP has not publicly confirmed following itself.
sections.strategy: JLP unveiled a three-year turnaround plan internally called "Rise", led by partnership chair Jason Tarry, targeting over £100m in additional profit by joining up John Lewis and Waitrose loyalty schemes plus £180m in annual profit from retail media. The group is also overhauling its digital strategy, reportedly treating AI shopping agents as a customer segment in their own right. John Lewis managing director Peter Ruis is stepping down, with Will Kernan taking over ahead of peak trading.
sections.launches: AW26 own-brand collections lean into tailoring and premium texture, with cashmere pieces starting at £69 and fig and olive as headline seasonal colours. Partner brands on the shop floor include 3.1 Phillip Lim, Topshop, Aligne and an exclusive Amanda Wakeley capsule. JLP also opened its online Christmas shop over 100 days early and confirmed 10,400 seasonal roles (6,000 at Waitrose, 2,600 at John Lewis) plus a new in-store restaurant concept called Platter.
sections.gossip: Interim results showed the loss before tax and exceptional items widening to £89m for the 26 weeks to 1 August, versus £34m a year earlier, with John Lewis sales down 2% to £2.0bn as discretionary spending stayed weak — the backdrop against which the "Rise" plan and MD change are landing.
soWhat: Widening H1 losses (£89m vs £34m) alongside a profit-extraction-focused turnaround plan point to continued cost pressure being pushed down the supply chain — expect harder-nosed cost negotiations into 2027 buying cycles.

The new Mirakl supplier platform and faster-onboarding model (see Russell & Bromley) signal JLP is actively opening doors to new, agile brand partners outside its traditional wholesale process — a potential entry point for suppliers who aren't already on the roster.

AW26's push on accessible premium (cashmere from £69, tailoring, fig/olive palette) confirms continued appetite for quality wool and cotton at competitive cost points — relevant for RWS wool and premium cotton suppliers pitching into the John Lewis own-brand range.

No fresh sourcing-country or nearshoring commitments this week suggests JLP's India/Portugal/Turkey/UK mix is currently stable rather than shifting — worth re-checking after leadership settles under the new MD and full 'Rise' plan detail emerges.
